quizName:
Hardest Questions in New york
									  					
									  														  					Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that right turns are not allowed in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right to cross at crosswalks, both marked and unmarked. You must stop for them when they are crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes will soon become one. Be ready to merge with other traffic.

questions.question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to calm down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions make it hard to drive safely. Wait until you feel calm before you drive. You need to focus on the road, not on what upset you.

questions.question: In New York, who must wear seat belts in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: All adults must wear seat belts. All children must be in a seat belt, booster seat, or car seat. Not wearing a seat belt can result in a fine up to $100.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and damages your judgment—just like alcohol and drugs do.

questions.question: What can happen if you drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs?

options.text: Your driver license can be taken away.

questions.explanation: Driving under the influence can result in fines, jail time, and loss of your driver license.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than daytime driving?

options.text: You cannot see as well in the dark.
Rain is more likely at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can see less of the road. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle immediately. Move it out of traffic if you can. Call the police and an ambulance if needed. Help stop any serious bleeding. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
questions.explanation: This round sign warns of a railroad crossing ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Drivers should slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may go. Let any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection pass first. Go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when signs, warning devices, or flaggers alert you to a train. It is illegal to go around lowered gates.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions per mile. You must focus fully on driving. Any other activity can be dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This orange sign warns of roadwork coming up. Stay alert for temporary traffic signs in work zones.

questions.question: What should a driver do before taking a non-prescription drug and driving?

options.text: Drive no matter what the label says.

questions.explanation: Over-the-counter drugs like cold and allergy medicine can affect your driving. Always check the label for warnings. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Drive faster to get there sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: You are too tired to drive safely if your eyes are closing, you drift between lanes, or you need to turn up the radio to stay awake. Stop at a safe place to rest.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Driving too fast for the conditions

questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can lead to hitting other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful near children. Always let pedestrians in a crosswalk cross first.

questions.question: What should you do if you see animals near the road?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Quickly swerve to the next lane.

questions.explanation: Slow down if you see animals near the road. They may run or change direction suddenly. Animals often travel in groups, so more may be nearby out of sight.
